subtype: Approach: keeps asking why until a deeper cause appears [Thinking]
passage: Teacher's note. Kashish had lost her pencil box for the third time this term. This time I asked her not to look for it first, but to ask 'why' out loud. 'Why do I lose it?' 'I leave it at school.' 'Why do I leave it?' 'I rush at the bell.' 'Why do I rush?' Kashish thought for a while. 'Because I only start packing when the bell rings, and Chinmay is already waiting at the door.' She grinned. 'So I should pack before the bell.' The next day Kashish began packing five minutes early. By Friday the box came home every day.

qa.q: How many times had Kashish lost the pencil box this term?
qa.a: Kashish had lost the pencil box for the third time this term.
Kashish's grin suggested she was pleased, since she had found the cause and a plan of her own.

qa.q: What other step could help Kashish remember the box?
qa.a: Kashish could keep a small picture card in her bag listing what to pack, since a card reminds her even on rushed days.

qa.q: How might Chinmay have seen Kashish packing early?
qa.a: Chinmay was probably glad to leave without waiting at the door, since Kashish was ready when the bell rang.

grounding: Shows a girl who keeps losing her pencil box asking why again and again until she finds the deeper cause and packs before the bell.
